modelResponse.episodeSummary: Walter J. Osei, 70M, Complete Heart Block, critical, hypotensive
keyECGEvidence: morphology: AV dissociation; wide QRS escape; tall peaked symmetric T waves; flattened P waves
preEventNote: Progressive PR prolongation then AV dissociation; QRS widening over 20 min
modelResponse.mechanism: Hyperkalemia causes conduction system block (AV node and His-Purkinje system) and myocardial toxicity, leading to AV dissociation and bradycardia.

rejectedAlternatives.why: No ST deviation or specific ischemic morphology mentioned; primary driver is severe electrolyte abnormality.
No digoxin level provided; ECG findings (peaked T waves, wide QRS) are classic for hyperkalemia, not digoxin toxicity.
Acute onset with progressive PR prolongation and QRS widening in the context of missed dialysis and critical hyperkalemia points strongly to an electrolyte cause.

recommendedActions: Administer Calcium Gluconate 1g IV push (for membrane stabilization)
Administer Sodium Bicarbonate 100 mEq IV push (for acidosis and intracellular K+ shift)
Administer Insulin 10 units IV with Dextrose 50g IV (for intracellular K+ shift)
Consider transcutaneous pacing if hemodynamically unstable or unresponsive to medical therapy
uncertainty: Exact timing of last potassium measurement relative to ECG capture.
Presence of other potential contributing factors not captured in data.
